page.layout: Running head at top centre with page number at top right; below, a centred title in two lines with the roman numeral XXXVIII at the end; a woodcut illustration in the middle; below it, a block of six lines of verse in italic with a large initial L; a faint catchword-like mark at the bottom left, not transcribed.

main_text.l: Luna Soli subiecta, lumen illius terris

l.i: Qua tamen admoti spectans tunc lumina
Sic periisse pij vulgo qui morte videntur,
Ipso qui potius Christo propiore potiti,

page.notes: The woodcut shows the sun at top, a small moon between sun and earth, and the earth in the centre, within two concentric circles, with trees and hills at the sides. The initial L of the verse is large. The first verse line has "coniuncta" with a long-s style spelling as printed: "coniunýta" is read as coniuncta. The mark at the lower left (faint printed letters) is not clearly legible and is omitted.
